title: ScreenSpot-v2: 4 wrong answer boxes and 1 duplicate case
body:
Hi, and thanks for ScreenSpot-v2. While benchmarking a model on it I looked at the cases the model missed, and found a few labels that look wrong. Below is everything with file names and indices, so it's easy to check.

Indices are 0-based positions in `screenspot_{mobile,desktop,web}_v2.json` from the HF dataset. Boxes are `[x, y, w, h]` in original pixels, as stored.

## 1. Answer boxes on the wrong element

**mobile [458]** `mobile_6edzq7.jpg` (1280x2774)
- Instruction: "switch on automatic downloads using cellular data"
- Stored bbox: `[26, 1095, 267, 136]`
- That's exactly the bbox of mobile [455] (`mobile_51nu75.png`, "switch to uppercase input"), where it marks the "abc" key. On this screenshot it lands on empty space next to the Wireless Data icon. It looks copied from [455].
- The target is the Automatic Downloads toggle under CELLULAR DATA. Suggested: `[1010, 2458, 150, 93]` (measured by eye).

![mobile 455 vs 458](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_mobile_455_458_copied_bbox.png)
![mobile 458 close-up](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_mobile_458_closeup.png)

**mobile [487]** `mobile_q24p8x.png` (2360x1640)
- Instruction: "switch the temperature display to Fahrenheit"
- Stored bbox: `[509, 228, 490, 80]`, the Notifications row of the menu.
- The target is the Fahrenheit row, two rows down. Suggested: `[509, 425, 490, 80]` (measured by eye, same size as the stored box).

![mobile 487](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_mobile_487_fahrenheit.png)

**web [200]** `web_d9841866-2ee7-4afd-a77a-8c0e52f6691c.png` (2560x1440)
- Instruction: "log in by x account"
- Stored bbox: `[2118, 476, 71, 59]`, the YouTube icon.
- The X icon is two icons to the left. ScreenSpot v1 has this same case with `[1979, 475, 71, 62]`, which is on the X icon. Suggested: restore the v1 box.

![web 200](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_web_200_x_account.png)

**web [202]** `web_11acd5dc-63ab-415f-823d-10cd68acef01.png` (2560x1440)
- Instruction: "check the weather news"
- Stored bbox: `[841, 307, 235, 104]`, the "DelmarvaLife" menu item.
- The Weather item is two to the left. ScreenSpot v1 has `[257, 306, 170, 109]` for this case, which is on Weather. Suggested: restore the v1 box.

![web 202](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_web_202_weather.png)

For web [200] and [202], v1 was right and the box changed in v2. Only 9 boxes changed between v1 and v2 for the same image and instruction, so these two may be worth a look together with the others.

## 2. Duplicate case

**web [182]** and **web [186]** are identical: same image (`web_e22bd6de-3985-4ccc-a316-eb383a03475f.png`), same instruction ("open the menu"), same bbox `[16, 21, 92, 83]`. v1 has this case once.

![web 182 and 186](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_web_182_186_duplicate.png)

## 3. A box 1 px past the image edge (harmless)

**mobile [449]** `mobile_02e9bl.png` (2360x1640), "view the photo pictured in Apr 11". The bbox `[645, 625, 1716, 965]` ends at x = 2361, one pixel past the 2360 px width. It doesn't change any score; just noting it in case someone validates boxes strictly.

![mobile 449](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_mobile_449_edge.png)

## 4. Judgment calls (opinions, unlike the above)

Separately, 39 of the missed cases have an instruction that I think fits another element about as well as the key: 18 with two valid answers, 12 where the key covers only part of one control (for example a radio dot but not its label), 8 loosely worded, and 1 I couldn't verify. These are opinions, and any of them could reasonably stay as they are. Three examples:

- **mobile [89]** "view more information" (`mobile_8da8fbf4-c2b0-495f-88d3-9eb682c15ce7.png`). The key is the ... button `[1035, 164, 86, 86]`. On the same screenshot, mobile [91] "view more information about classical christmas" uses the MORE link `[976, 1591, 147, 74]`, so the MORE link also fits "view more information".
- **web [196]** "create a new page" (`web_533f02b1-e687-462f-9d14-5a25f54d9464.png`). The key is the "Create this page" button `[96, 372, 297, 86]`. The sidebar has a link that reads exactly "Create new page".
- **web [401]** "Choose to sort from oldest to newest" (`web_dkh41m.png`). The key `[1099, 587, 24, 27]` covers only the radio dot. Clicking the "Oldest → Newest" label selects the same option.

![mobile 89 and 91](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_mobile_89_91_more_information.png)
![web 196](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_web_196_create_page.png)
![web 401](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/arthurkatcher/fb23967a36431273b6c6b89553b79880/raw/c067f1799b667273fd67e346cd6cdc559aae5196/fig_web_401_radio_label.png)

Happy to share the full list with screenshots if it's useful.

## Scope

I only looked at the cases one model missed, so this isn't a full audit of the dataset. Since every published score uses the current key, a small errata file next to the dataset might be easier than changing the key in place. People could then report both numbers.

**transformer：**
model = Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    "/root/autodl-tmp/OS-Copilot/OS-Atlas-Base-7B", torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto"
)

messages = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {
                "type": "image",
                "image": "/root/autodl-tmp/web_6f93090a-81f6-489e-bb35-1a2838b18c01.png",
                "min_pixels": 56 * 56,
                "max_pixels": 1280 * 28 * 28,
            },
            {"type": "text", "text": "In this UI screenshot, what is the position of the element corresponding to the command \"switch language of current page\" (with bbox)?"},
        ],
    }
]


# Preparation for inference

    messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
)
image_inputs, video_inputs = process_vision_info(messages)
inputs = processor(
    text=[text],
    images=image_inputs,
    videos=video_inputs,
    padding=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
)
inputs = inputs.to("cuda")

generated_ids_trimmed = [
    out_ids[len(in_ids):] for in_ids, out_ids in zip(inputs.input_ids, generated_ids)
]

output_text = processor.batch_decode(
    generated_ids_trimmed, skip_special_tokens=False, clean_up_tokenization_spaces=False

title: Clarification on SCROLL direction labeling (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT)
body:
Hi, thank you for your great work.

I have a question regarding how scroll directions are defined in the dataset.
In the paper, it's mentioned that scroll actions are labeled as:
SCROLL [DIRECTION (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT)]

It also seems that both traditional scroll (vertical movement) and swipe (horizontal movement) gestures are unified under this SCROLL action type.
However, the labeling standard for direction is not fully clear, specifically:
Are directions based on finger movement or screen movement?
For example, does SCROLL DOWN mean the finger moved up (so the screen moved down)?
Or is it the opposite?

We couldn’t find an explicit explanation of this in the paper or preprocessing scripts. If there is a standard or reference implementation that defines how these directions are derived from gesture coordinates (e.g., start and end points), it would be very helpful to know.

Thanks in advance!

title: OS-ATLAS-7B-Pro sometimes fails to output low-level operation
body:
Thanks for open-sourcing such a powerful model!

When testing OS-ATLAS-7B-Pro using the provided prompts in [https://github.com/OS-Copilot/OS-Atlas/blob/main/eval/data/omniact_test.jsonl](https://github.com/OS-Copilot/OS-Atlas/blob/main/eval/data/omniact_test.jsonl), I found that the model sometimes outputs the thoughts or the contents after `action:` was an action description instead of the executable action command.

For example:
```'thoughts:\nOpen Safeway app.'```
```'thoughts:\nClick on "What the fossil fuel industry doesn't want you to know" View.'\nactions:\nClick on "What the fossil fuel industry doesn't want you to know" View.''```

The prompt I used is as follows:
```
You are a foundational action model capable of automating tasks across various digital environments, including desktop systems like Windows, macOS, and Linux, as well as mobile platforms such as Android and iOS. You also excel in web browser environments. You will interact with digital devices in a human-like manner: by reading screenshots, analyzing them, and taking appropriate actions.

Your expertise covers two types of digital tasks:
    - Grounding: Given a screenshot and a description, you assist users in locating elements mentioned. Sometimes, you must infer which elements best fit the description when they aren't explicitly stated.
    - Executable Language Grounding: With a screenshot and task instruction, your goal is to determine the executable actions needed to complete the task.


You are now operating in Executable Language Grounding mode. Your goal is to help users accomplish tasks by suggesting executable actions that best fit their needs. Your skill set includes both basic and custom actions:

1. Basic Actions
Basic actions are standardized and available across all platforms. They provide essential functionality and are defined with a specific format, ensuring consistency and reliability. 
Basic Action 1: CLICK 
    - purpose: Click at the specified position.
    - format: CLICK <point>[[x-axis, y-axis]]</point>
    - example usage: CLICK <point>[[101, 872]]</point>
       
Basic Action 2: TYPE
    - purpose: Enter specified text at the designated location.
    - format: TYPE [input text]
    - example usage: TYPE [Shanghai shopping mall]

Basic Action 3: SCROLL
    - purpose: SCROLL in the specified direction.
    - format: SCROLL [direction (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT)]
    - example usage: SCROLL [UP]

2.Custom Actions
Custom actions are unique to each user's platform and environment. They allow for flexibility and adaptability, enabling the model to support new and unseen actions defined by users. These actions extend the functionality of the basic set, making the model more versatile and capable of handling specific tasks.


Custom Action 1: PRESS_BACK
    - purpose: Press a back button to navigate to the previous screen.
    - format: PRESS_BACK
    - example usage: PRESS_BACK

Custom Action 2: PRESS_HOME
    - purpose: Press a home button to navigate to the home page.
    - format: PRESS_HOME
    - example usage: PRESS_HOME

Custom Action 3: OPEN_APP
    - purpose: Open the specified application.
    - format: OPEN_APP [app_name]
    - example usage: OPEN_APP [Google Chrome]

Custom Action 4: WAIT
    - purpose: Wait for the screen to load.
    - format: WAIT
    - example usage: WAIT

Custom Action 5: COMPLETE
    - purpose: Indicate the task is finished.
    - format: COMPLETE
    - example usage: COMPLETE

In most cases, task instructions are high-level and abstract. Carefully read the instruction and action history, then perform reasoning to determine the most appropriate next action. Ensure you strictly generate two sections: Thoughts and Actions.
Thoughts: Clearly outline your reasoning process for current step.
Actions: Specify the actual actions you will take based on your reasoning. You should follow action format above when generating. 

Your current task instruction, action history, and associated screenshot are as follows:
Screenshot:
```

The task instruction is like:
```
Task: In the Flipboard App, go to the search bar, type podcast, and listen to the first result podcast.
History: 
Step 1: Click on "podcast" TextView.
Step 2: Click on the #podcasts.
Step 3: Click on "What the fossil fuel industry doesn't want you to know" View.
```

Could the authors provide some hints about how to tackle this issue?

title: Catastrophic forgetting when trying to fine-tune OS-ATLAS-Base-7B on grounding
body:
Hi, 

Thanks for the great work. While I have been able to get inference on the pre-trained OS-ATLAS-Base-7B to work, when I try to fine-tune the model using LLaMA-factory using various settings (frozen ViT layer, lower learning rate, etc.) on additional custom grounding data following the exact prompt and data format mentioned in the inference code, I observe that the performance goes down very significantly on grounding benchmarks like Screenspot even though the train loss goes down. Do you know why this might be happening?

Thank you.

title: Batched inference for `OS-Atlas-Base-7B` is broken with `attn_implementation="flash_attention_2"`
body:
Hi, it seems like batched inference is broken when flash_attention is used. When running inference on the 1st example of ScreenSpot test example with flash_attention_2, the output changes depending on the batch size

* Batch_size = 1: `<|object_ref_start|>close button<|object_ref_end|><|box_start|>(954,148),(988,196)<|box_end|><|im_end|>`

* Batch_size = 4: `降序<|im_end|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|><|endoftext|>`

When I disable flash attention_2, the results look fine.

* Batch_size = 1: `<|object_ref_start|>close button<|object_ref_end|><|box_start|>(954,148),(988,196)<|box_end|><|im_end|>`

* Batch_size = 4: `<|object_ref_start|>close button<|object_ref_end|><|box_start|>(954,148),(988,196)<|box_end|><|im_end|>`

Flash attention with batch_size=1 is fast enough so this bug is not a deal breaker for me, although it'd be nice if this is addressed.
